name: H5N1 bird flu
value: US H5N1 death (1 Nov); no human spread
summary: Washington State reports first US H5N1 death of 2026; three cattle-linked cases since mid-October
state: A Yakima County resident exposed to infected dairy cattle died of H5N1 on 1 Nov, the first US bird flu death of 2026 (Contagion Live). Washington has recorded three human cases since mid-October, all linked to infected cows on dairies where 33 herds are infected. The CDC rates the public risk as low and has found no person-to-person spread (CNN). Cases remain animal-linked as of 5 Nov.
for_you: The risk to the public is low. People who work with poultry or dairy cattle should follow UKHSA or CDC guidance.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only, no human clusters = Normal

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
